findings: Configured results_dir is resolved before the no-script/no-Lake compatibility branch; existing unresolved history is not erased by optional argument omission.
Public training/posthoc launches and native intent writers check pre-script history before their resource/attempt creation; writer checks occur inside the existing authority transaction.

A native false result delivers its captured full pre-script Ref to the separate failure action then continues the scheduler loop without calling the legacy fixer. A stale report likewise cannot fall through to launch.
Genuinely legacy bool-returning pre-script/fixer behavior is not reclassified as new supervision. The slice adds no mandatory setup to no-history direct APIs.
Source verification is scope-only and does not recursively call the launch-ready gate, permitting legitimate failed-source reporting and exact duplicate checks at the new FAILED fence.

doc_review.limits: Clearly scoped to native project pre-script: cooperative CPU environment, Linux owned tree proof, no input/output sandbox, no automatic fixer/artifacts/observations/restart adoption or general CPU research loop.

limitations: This report does not claim independent review of the reporter it authored; the other agent supplies that review.
No full-suite result is claimed here. Root's later full inventory and canonical evidence own final aggregate acceptance.

Filesystem effects are not rolled back. SQL/final readback failures after prepare retain uncertain ownership and may leave FAILED metrics or a zero-allocation receipt while the task remains CLAIMED; neither is permission for repair or replay.

Claim ID and pre-script occurrence ID are distinct. Zero-allocation reporting refuses an existing start and never overwrites an allocation. This is admission accounting, not measured CPU/GPU efficiency.
The immutable source effect is historical evidence, not freshly adopted process authority. Duplicate reporting requires the same current source and exact raw claim plus current FAILED action fence.
